issues.failure_explanation: A_{z_0} is defined as a subset of Omega^infty_X, so it only contains continuous nonsingular maps. The set B constrains only null-set conditions omega(R(F,c,r))=0 and never imposes F_#omega << omega. For a non-nonsingular continuous F these conditions depend on the chosen representatives and are not about K_F, so proj(B) can contain maps outside A_{z_0}. The equality A_{z_0}=proj(B) is therefore not proved. Analyticity of A_{z_0} would need B intersected with a Borel (or analytic) set of nonsingular maps, and the proof never shows that this set is Borel or analytic.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Show that {F : F_#omega << omega} is Borel in C(X,X) (via the continuous map F -> F_#omega into the Polish space of finite measures), and intersect B with it.
issues.overall_effect: The upper bound in the Sigma^1_1-completeness claim (part (b) of thm:route-IF-to-Az0) is unsupported as written. Non-Borelness (the hardness direction) is unaffected.
issues.title: Analyticity proof does not enforce nonsingularity, so proj(B) is not A_{z_0}
issues.why_classification: The missing fact is a routine descriptive-set-theory observation, and the SCI lower-bound arguments need only hardness, so every substantive claim survives.

issues.failure_explanation: u_m(S) is built by a one-pass greedy extension of u_{m-1}(S), and failure (bot) is absorbing. Choosing a star early does not guarantee that a maximal pattern survives, so the claim that u_m(S) has at least as many stars as any admissible witness is false. Counterexample: let S be the downward closure of {strings starting with 0} together with the string '1'. Then S contains the Silver tree S_{A,x} with A={0}, x(0)=0, and A is coinfinite, so S is in V. Greedy gives u_1=* because {0,1} lies in S. At level 2 none of **, *0, *1 is admissible, because 10 and 11 are not in S. Hence u_m=bot for all m>=2 and k_m(S)=0 for m>=2, so k_m is bounded. By the paper's own Step 1 of lem:reverse_r3D1_SilverKoopman, z_0 is then not in sigma_ap(K_{F_S}), although S is in V. The forward implication, and therefore the equivalence S in V iff z_0 in sigma_ap, is false for the constructed Psi. The 1-Lipschitz version def:Psi-Lip uses the same u_m(S) and has the same defect.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows that lambda has small lower-norm residual sigma_inf(K_j-lambda)<=2 eps_n for blocks j(n), i.e. lambda lies in an eps-approximate-point pseudospectrum of the block. Such a pseudospectral point need not lie near sigma_ap of that block, because the blocks are non-normal and the proof gives no uniform resolvent bound. Counterexample to (iii) as stated: take blocks that are chains i -> i-1 on {1..N}, N=1,2,..., with the end point fixed. Each block has sigma_ap contained in {0,1}, but sigma_inf(K_N-1/2)->0 as N grows. The l^infty-sum then has 1/2 in sigma_ap, which is not in the closure of the union {0,1}. So the stated equality sigma_ap = closure of union is false in general.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict (iii) to the superset inclusion, which is valid and is all that is needed for the forward direction. For the subset inclusion, add a hypothesis of uniformly bounded resolvents on the blocks, for example cycles of bounded length. Prove it from the explicit finite-order resolvent formula (norm at most L(1+|lambda|)^{L-1}/|1-lambda^L|) and apply it with bounded k_m in the reverse step.
issues.overall_effect: The upper inclusion of sigma_ap(K_{F_S}) into the closure of the union of root-of-unity sets rests on an unproved general lemma. It is used in the reverse implication when k_m is bounded. The inclusion is probably true there because the cycle lengths are bounded, but that is not what is proved.
